Now, we must only keep the solutions that are in the domain of the logarithms in the original inequality. To find the domain of the logarithms, we recall that the argument of the logarithm must be positive:

Our solution is $x \leq \dfrac{2}{3e^5-1},$ which can be expressed as $\left( -\infty, \dfrac{2}{3e^5-1} \right].$ Additionally, the domains of the logarithms are $x > -2$ and $x>0,$ which can be expressed as $(-2,\infty)$ and $(0,\infty)$ respectively. To find the solutions that are in the domains of the logarithms, we take the intersection:

\[ \left( -\infty, \dfrac{2}{3e^5-1} \right] \cap (-2, \infty) \cap (0, \infty) = \left( 0, \dfrac{2}{3e^5-1} \right] \]

Now, we use each side of the inequality as an exponent of $e.$ We get the following:

\[\begin{align*} e^{\ln(x-2)} &\geq e^{-6} \\[5pt] x-2 &\geq e^{-6} \\[5pt] x &\geq e^{-6}+2 \\[5pt] x &\geq \dfrac{1+2e^6}{e^6} \end{align*}\]

\[ \left[ \dfrac{1+2e^6}{e^6}, \infty \right) \cap (2, \infty) = \left[ \dfrac{1+2e^6}{e^6}, \infty \right) \]

example.title: Solving an Inequality Involving One Logarithmic Function

Now, we use each side of the inequality as an exponent of $10.$ We get the following: \begin{align} {10}^{\log(4x-6)} & \leq 10^{1} \\[5pt] 4x-6 &\leq 10 \\[5pt] 4x & \leq 16\\[5pt] x & \leq 4 \end{align}

Now, we must only keep the solutions that are in the domain of the logarithm in the original inequality. To find the domain of the logarithm, we recall that the argument of the logarithm must be positive: \[ 4x-6 > 0 \quad \Rightarrow \quad x > \dfrac{3}{2} \]

Our solution is $x \leq 4,$ which can be expressed as $\left( -\infty, 4\right].$ Additionally, the domain of the logarithm is $x > \dfrac{3}{2},$ which can be expressed as $\left(\dfrac{3}{2},\infty\right).$ To find the solutions that are in the domain of the logarithm, we take the intersection: \[ \left( -\infty, 4 \right] \cap \left(\dfrac{3}{2},\infty\right) = \left(\dfrac{3}{2}, 4 \right] \]

\[ \left[\dfrac{4-e^3}{2+e^3}, \infty \right) \cap (-1, \infty) \cap (-\infty, 2) = \left[\dfrac{4-e^3}{2+e^3}, 2 \right) \]
